The official lstlean.tex taken from the link on the page here defines the symbol ▸ twice.
First

{▸}{{\ensuremath{\blacktriangleright}}}1

then 

{▸}{{\ensuremath{\triangleright}}}1

The fist one is a filled black triangle like in the \rw cast, the second is a non-filled triangle and im not sure why it is there. It overwrites the first definition though.
The second one might be related to normal subgroups, no?
Does Mathlib use the non-filled out version for that?
It is not an abbreviation in Mathlib, but I can see it used in papers about Lean.

If someone wants ▷ as output, then they should also use ▷ as input in the code block, not ▸.
I.e. they should add {▷}{{\ensuremath{\triangleright}}}1 to this file.

And furthermore, if it isn't even notation for code in Mathlib, then it has no business to be in a file that is explicitly for valid lean code highlighting, let alone overwrite a symbol which actually is valid lean code
(▸ is the casting symbol \rw and comes from core)

Also lstlisting errors out (even on a completely harmless lstlisting) if a listing happens to be at a page break (if you use hyperref) because we set 

extendedchars=false,

see
https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/690832/argument-of-has-an-extra-error-from-listings-hyperref

The error is 

Argument of � has an extra }.

also one should probably set the default value of automatically linebreaked lines to 

breakindent=2\fontdimen2\font,

(which corresponds to 2 spaces)
since it is most likely that the assumptions are getting linebreaked.
The current (default) value of lstlistings corresponds to something between 4 and 5 spaces which looks off
You can avoid many of these issues by switching to xelatex+juliamono+minted :)
(as of about 6 months ago ArXiv supports xelatex so I've been encouraging everyone to switch to minted)

Do you have any special minted setup to make the highlighting slightly more coloful?
E.g. tactics like apply and exact aren't even colored by default.

Minted uses Pygments for lexing.

The lexer for Lean is defined here: https://github.com/pygments/pygments/blob/98aa256034403c29cf49d8ec5d190002e0fc1c85/pygments/lexers/lean.py
Documentation on writing lexers: https://pygments.org/docs/lexerdevelopment/

You can probably achieve what you have in mind by simply adding more keywords.
I hope we keep the lstlistings file around and maintain it since (at least) LNCS still doesn't support xelatex.
